paragraphs.text: Open and drive every dsh on your tailnet from any dsh, with a complete phone layout.
Kivotos

English ·
简体中文 ·
日本語 ·
한국어
Every DeepSeek Harness you run, from any computer or your phone.
Kivotos is an open source plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Open any of your machines' dsh from any
other, with its full UI: sessions, approvals, models, settings, files, and terminal. It adds a phon
e layout to dsh and comes with an Android app.
- **All your machines:** Switch between them from the dsh sidebar. What you see is the remote dsh's

own UI, so everything works.
- **Two ways to connect:** Tailscale, or a relay server you run yoursel

f. A machine can use both at once.
- **Untrusted relay:** The relay only forwards end-to-end encrypt

ed data. It cannot read it or join your network.
- **Phone layout:** Drawer sidebar, composer at the

bottom, safe areas, light and dark.
- **Android app:** The full dsh UI, with notifications for appr
ovals, questions, and finished tasks; an approval that maps to one tool call can be allowed or denie

d right from the notification.
- **Safe restart:** Restart dsh from anywhere, even when you are only

connected remotely: it quits cleanly, starts again by itself, and the page reconnects.
- **Self-hos
ted:** No account, no telemetry, no push service.
## Getting Started
### Prerequisites

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` (`>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0-0`)
- Tailscale signed in to the same account
on every device, or your own relay server
### Plugin
Install it on every machine. In dsh, open **Plugins → Install a third-party plugin** and enter `kivo
tos`. Or from the terminal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart dsh. Your other machines appear under **Machines** at the bottom of the sidebar.
### Phone
Install the APK from the releases page. On the computer, open **Machines → Pair phone** and scan the
rom the releases page. On the computer, open **Machines → Pair phone** and scan the code in the app.
### Relay
Run the relay with Docker Compose on a server with a public address:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
On the first computer, open **Settings → Remote access → Own relay**, enter the relay's address, and
create a network. Register it on the relay by running the command the page shows after `docker comp
ose exec relay`. Other computers and phones join with the invite link or its QR code.
The session event stream (`/api/remote.mux`) is compressed with `permessage-deflate` wherever both e
nds support it. With dsh 0.2.2 or newer the browser and dsh negotiate it end to end and Kivotos pass
es the frames through unchanged; with an older dsh Kivotos compresses the hop to the browser itself
(off when it would not help). A 600 KB history snapshot costs about a third of its bytes on a thrott
led link. The extension is per message with context takeover off, and messages under 1 KB are left a
lone. Set `muxCompression: "off"` in the plugin config to disable it; the CPU cost is one deflate/in
flate per large message on the computer serving the page.
A relay connection that drops only takes that connection down: the computer reconnects with backoff,
and a dropped session closes by itself. On a link whose network queue can run longer than the relay
's 20 s ping (`relaySilenceSeconds`, default 70 s) the control connection can be declared dead late;
the plugin config key `relaySilenceSeconds` (30..600) raises it.
Anyone with the invite link, or signed in to your Tailscale account, has full control of your machin
one with the invite link, or signed in to your Tailscale account, has full control of your machines.
### Restarting dsh remotely
Quitting dsh would also end the connection you are using, so Kivotos restarts it for you: **Machines
→ Restart dsh…** (on a computer and on the phone), or type `/kivotos restart` in a conversation (`n
ow`, `idle` (the default), `status`, `cancel`). The dialog lists what is running and offers **Restar
t when idle** or **Restart now**. dsh quits cleanly, a helper process starts it again and checks tha
t Kivotos answers (retrying the launch up to three times), and the page reconnects by itself and sho
ws which plugins changed. If something goes wrong, the helper's log is at `$DSH_HOME/kivotos/restart
/restart.log`. Supported for the macOS desktop app and for `dsh web` started from a terminal; not on
Windows or under systemd.
## Development

- `packages/kivotos`: the dsh plugin (TypeScript)
- `packages/mobile`: the Android app (Expo, Kotlin

)
- `packages/relay`: the relay server (Go)
